attribution: Rombert Stapel, Historical Atlas of the Low Countries (1350–1800), v15, DataverseNL, doi:10.34894/BTKFHV. ADM1 display grouping and tile-grid conversion by World History Atlas.
meaning: Display/directory groups of original localities with identical full ADM1 strings; not national boundaries or single-sovereignty claims.
numericId: First 13 hexadecimal digits (52 bits) of the complete ADM1 SHA256; stable gid string also retained in properties

conversion.inputGrid: Original source projected and independently quantized at each zoom using the same locality-MVT grid, extent and buffer
conversion.union: Clear precision model without moving quantized coordinates; union per full ADM1 string with grid_size=0; no second union snap
conversion.clipping: Per-group polygon intersection with buffered tile rectangle at grid_size=1, followed by standard MVT encoding
conversion.note: Tile clipping re-quantizes union intersection nodes to the tile integer grid. This is not identical to the canonical floating-coordinate union everywhere, nor always associative with per-locality clipping. No manual repairs or smoothing.
conversion.sharedBoundaries: Each query polygon retains its own boundary. Visible edges use a separate unique line network; draw halc_region_edges uniformly instead of stroking each polygon.
conversion.edgeNetwork: Global group boundaries are unioned at grid_size=1, line-merged, clipped on the tile grid, unioned at grid_size=1 again to deduplicate snapped coincidences, and line-merged. This line conversion may differ from ghost polygon boundaries by grid quantization; no tile-frame boundaries are invented. Group memberships remain unchanged.
